clue.text: A scrupulous person, and a persistent one, about money

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the persistent one goes round the money

parts.note: something that sticks fast is a sticker
L stands for pound (libra), a unit of money

explanation.surface: A fussy, tenacious person haggling over cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who insists on every rule or detail is a pedant about exactness.

clue.text: Persevering type is about satisfied with verse

indicators.note: about means the persevering type goes around the word for satisfied

parts.note: a trier is someone who keeps trying
met means satisfied, as in met demands

explanation.surface: A determined person contented with poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of three metrical feet is a form of poetic line.

clue.text: Argument against writing to one concerning a war-time measure

parts.note: a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons
script is writing
I is the Roman numeral for one
on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Objections to a letter concerning wartime policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Compulsory enlistment into the armed forces is a policy adopted in war.

clue.text: One allowed to make bargains?

parts.note: read as a person holding a permit to trade, such as a publican licensed to sell drink

explanation.surface: Asking who is permitted to strike deals.
explanation.definitionFit: A holder of a permit, such as a pub landlord, has official permission to trade.

clue.text: Day-dreaming parson on the lake

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a title for a clergyman
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A vicar lost in thought beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of absent musing is a waking dream.

clue.text: Mulled and spiced wine on board?

explanation.surface: Hot spiced wine served aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship; the board is a chessboard, where this piece moves diagonally.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot spiced punch shares its name with the mitred chess piece found on the chessboard.

clue.text: Some uppish gunners in training

indicators.note: in means the reversed gunners go inside the training

parts.note: PT is physical training

indicators.note: uppish in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

explanation.surface: A few cocky artillerymen at drill.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion of a whole is a share of it.

clue.text: He was associated with the cabinet in Pitt's day

definitions.text: He was associated with the cabinet in Pitt's day

parts.words: He was associated with the cabinet in Pitt's day
parts.note: cabinet means a piece of furniture, not a government; a famous furniture designer worked when William Pitt was Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A politician who sat in the government under Pitt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' suggests the ministers of William Pitt the Younger, but it is furniture: Thomas Sheraton was a Georgian cabinet-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Sheraton was a Georgian furniture designer working in the 1790s, the era of Pitt the Younger.

clue.text: Point to Greek letter with curve in the inscription

parts.note: E is a compass point, east
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a graph is a plotted curve

explanation.surface: Instructions for carving a Greek letter and a curve on a monument.
explanation.definitionFit: A motto or quotation carved on a building or set at the head of a book is a kind of engraved text.

clue.text: Right position of course — north

parts.note: on a golf course the lie is where the ball rests

explanation.surface: A navigator confirming a ship's bearing to the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests a ship's heading, but it is a golf course: a ball's resting place is its lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal claim to hold another's property until a debt is paid is a kind of entitlement.

clue.text: Man of theatre has varied views

explanation.surface: An actor or critic whose opinions keep changing.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: a stagehand who moves scenery literally changes the views the audience sees.
explanation.definitionFit: A stagehand works backstage in a playhouse, and by moving scenery he alters what the audience looks at.

clue.text: A friend at the gathering appears timorous

indicators.note: gathering means the letters of A friend at the are collected up into a new order

explanation.surface: A companion at a party seems shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking courage and easily scared is cowardly or timid.

clue.text: Looks for a way up, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a flight of stairs is a way to climb up

explanation.surface: Someone peering about in search of a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: Gazes fixedly are long hard looks.

clue.text: It is to one law maker lawful, that goes without saying

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an MP (Member of Parliament) makes laws
licit means lawful

explanation.surface: A statement that a legislator's action is legal, which hardly needs stating.
explanation.definitionFit: Something understood though never stated outright is unspoken or tacit.

clue.text: Unusual issue of notes

parts.note: issue is offspring, and a rare birth brings three babies at once; in music a group of three notes played in the time of two has the same name

explanation.surface: A rare print run of banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' and 'notes' suggest money or publishing; issue means offspring and the notes are musical.
explanation.definitionFit: One of three born together is a rare kind of offspring, and three notes grouped together in music share the name.

clue.text: Message gives border rent rise

indicators.note: rise in a down clue means the words are read from the bottom up, so backwards

parts.note: marge is a poetic word for margin or border
to let is to rent out

explanation.surface: A notice that the landlord is raising the rent on a border plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns MARGELET round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wired communication was an urgent written dispatch.

clue.text: Scheme includes also some soldiers

indicators.note: includes means the scheme holds the word for also within it

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
too means also

explanation.surface: A plan that takes in a few troops as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A small military unit under a lieutenant is a group of troops.

clue.text: Duration of seven 24 on the world stage

definitions.text: Duration of seven 24 on the world stage

parts.words: Duration of seven 24 on the world stage
parts.note: 24 is the answer to 24-down, so seven of them echo Shakespeare's All the world's a stage, where a man's span is played in seven acts

explanation.surface: How long seven performances run on an international stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Jaques's speech in As You Like It says all the world's a stage, with a man's ages played in seven acts.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole time a person exists is, in Shakespeare's image, a play of seven acts.

clue.text: Offering an obol — it appears odd

indicators.note: odd means the letters of an obol and it are arranged strangely

explanation.surface: Someone finds giving a tiny Greek coin peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift presented to God or a deity is a religious sacrifice.

clue.text: Tales traditionally down to earth?

explanation.surface: Stories that are, by tradition, practical and unpretentious.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word in two: the ends of your legs, the feet, are what touch the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional stories are myths, and the feet at the base of the legs rest on the ground.

clue.text: Use some silk in one's suit?

definitions.text: Use some silk in one's suit?

parts.words: Use some silk in one's suit?
parts.note: silk is a senior barrister (one who takes silk), and a suit is a lawsuit, so this means go to law employing counsel

explanation.surface: A tailor advising silk for the lining of a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a senior barrister, a Queen's or King's Counsel, is called a silk.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a dispute to court is to pursue a lawsuit, often with a barrister.

clue.text: At which tramps may ride

parts.note: tramps are tramp steamers, cargo ships, and a moored ship is said to ride at it

explanation.surface: A place where vagrants hitch a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramps' suggests vagrants; a tramp is a cargo ship without a fixed route.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy weight dropped to hold a ship in place is what a moored vessel rides at.

clue.text: Henry IV's character very weak

explanation.surface: A judgement that a king's personality was spineless.
explanation.walkthrough: Francis Feeble is a recruit in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 2; 'character' suggests the king's nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare named a minor recruit for his frailty, and the word itself means lacking strength.

clue.text: Poetic hamlet in general, with church and spreading trees

parts.note: Ulysses S. Grant was a US Civil War general

indicators.note: spreading means the letters of trees are spread about into a new order

explanation.surface: A village scene with an army officer, a church and wide trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' rearranges TREES into ESTER. Grantchester is the village near Cambridge in Rupert Brooke's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A village near Cambridge celebrated in Rupert Brooke's poem is a small settlement famed in verse.

clue.text: Apostolic performances

explanation.surface: Shows put on by the disciples.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Testament book of the apostles shares its title with the word for deeds or stage turns.

clue.text: In. court, witness appears a fool?

indicators.note: In tells us the letters sit inside the words court and witness

explanation.surface: In the courtroom a witness makes himself look stupid.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray full stop after 'In' is an OCR mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A silly person is an idiot.

clue.text: Space traveller is given a hormone perhaps

parts.note: many hormones, such as testosterone, are steroids

explanation.surface: An astronaut being dosed with hormones.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor planet orbiting the sun is a rocky body moving through space.

clue.text: Sadness beginning during this sort of spree?

indicators.note: beginning picks the opening letter of the word Sadness

parts.note: pending can mean during, as in pending the inquiry

explanation.surface: Gloom setting in during a shopping binge.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopping binge is a splurge of paying out money.
